(1) INDEPENDENT ASSET RE-EXTRACTION. Re-parsed local_assets/roarm_m3/urdf/meshes/gripper_link.stl (sha256 7946a374…f65a56 verified, 13698 tris). Isolated the Y-normal web FRONT face (493 tris, all verts within 5e-3 of y=-5.9834), rasterised at 100 px/mm, took connected components of the complement not touching the border -> 6 through-holes. Reproduced the lead's table to <0.002 mm (B: 30.9212/-6.3735, 63.3912/-18.9335, 30.9212/-31.4935 r=1.5817; S: 38.3041/-8.4335, 38.3041/-29.4335 r=1.0843; flower centroid 51.1187/-18.9347 area 144.18 mm2). Added a 6th usable point: the flower's inscribed BORE, by iterative circle fit to the flower boundary near the distance-transform maximum -> centre (50.3181, -18.9331), r=5.1006 mm (Ø10.2012). NOTE the bore centre is 0.80 mm from the flower area-centroid (the flower is asymmetric in x), so these are different features.

(2) PHOTO TRIAGE. Viewed all six photos. Web plate identified face-on in p0 (apex left), p02 (apex up), p04 (apex down): all 6 holes visible in each. p01/p03/p05 rejected — steep obliquity and partial occlusion of the head.

(3) ESTIMATOR DESIGN + VALIDATION (this drove everything). First attempts failed: (a) whole-ROI Otsu segmentation broke because the plate is not the largest dark component and the ruler/shadows leak in; (b) a radial gradient-edge ellipse fit was unstable (two variants disagreed by up to 6 px). In p0 the holes are NOT bright-through-holes — they show a mid-grey disc against black plate. Settled on a HALF-MAX BLOB CENTROID: plate level L = median of the darkest 45% of an annulus at 1.35–2.10 r0 (robust to nearby bright regions — the first L estimate was contaminated by the plate edge near B2 and by the U-cut near S2), hole level H = median of a 0.45 r0 core, centroid averaged over thresholds L+{0.40,0.50,0.60}(H-L), iterated to convergence.
   Validated on synthetic renders modelling the real camera (f=2665 px, d=137 mm), plate tilt 0–30 deg, the 1.51 mm plate thickness producing WALL OCCLUSION (the far rim occludes part of the near opening), 6x supersampling, blur sigma 2.2, illumination gradient, noise. Result: image-plane distance-RATIO error rms 0.053%, max 0.18%. Crucially the wall-occlusion centre bias (up to 8.9 px = 0.46 mm) is 97–99% COMMON-MODE (a uniform translation, because for a flat plate it is a radial shrink about the principal point), so it cancels in pairwise distances. This is what makes the ratio test defensible.

(4) HOMOGRAPHY. Fitted H: asset plate (x,z) mm -> image px from the 6 correspondences (cv2.findHomography DLT + Levenberg–Marquardt on reprojection error). Residuals mapped back to plate mm via the local 2x2 Jacobian of H^-1. Both mirror labelings tried; they are exactly degenerate because the asset 6-hole set is mirror-symmetric about z=-18.9335.

(5) NULL AND POWER STUDY on synthetic renders of the ASSET design through the SAME pipeline: null residual RMS 0.011–0.028 mm; a single-hole design displacement delta raises residual RMS by ~0.21*delta (0.3 mm -> 0.063, 0.5 mm -> 0.106, 1.0 mm -> 0.216); a uniform scale s=1.03/1.10 is invisible (0.021 mm, = null) as expected; an ANISOTROPIC x-stretch k=1.03 is ALSO invisible (0.021 mm) — because a homography absorbs every affine map. That limitation forced step 6.

(6) METRIC ANISOTROPY CHECK. EXIF: samsung SM-S906N, 35mm-equiv 23 mm on a 4000x3000 frame -> f = 2657.9 px; Orientation=8 and cv2 auto-rotates, so the array is 3000x4000 and the principal point is (1500,2000). With K known, K^-1 H = lambda[r1 r2 t]; |r1|/|r2| must be 1 for a rigid plane carrying the asset design, and departs from 1 exactly when the real design is anisotropically stretched. Validated on synthetic: null 1.0086+-0.0054; x-stretch k=1.01/1.03/1.05 -> 1.0187/1.0384/1.0582 (1:1 tracking); uniform s=1.03 -> 1.0082 (correctly blind). Focal swept 2600–2720 px to check sensitivity.

(7) CROSS-PHOTO RESIDUAL-VECTOR CONSISTENCY. A genuine design offset must produce the SAME residual vector in plate coordinates in every photo; noise must not.

(8) OUTLINE TEST (many-DOF, independent). Warped the ENTIRE asset web boundary — outer outline + all six hole boundaries, ~5.5k sampled points, none of which entered the fit — and measured the offset to the real part's edge by a sub-pixel search for peak intensity gradient along the local normal (+-11 px), converting px->mm with the local Jacobian, discarding points with weak/ambiguous contrast (tine occlusion).

(9) A flower full-contour ICP was attempted and DISCARDED as invalid — see caveats.

WHAT THIS IMPLIES ABOUT PLATE IDENTITY:
1. Scale of the residual. 0.08–0.10 mm RMS on a 34.8146 mm baseline is 0.24–0.29%, and is smaller than one hole radius by a factor of ~16 (B holes r=1.58 mm) — far below the "small fraction of a hole diameter" bar. Even the worst photo (p02, plate tilted ~25 deg, one hole partly wall-occluded) stays at 0.30 mm RMS = 0.19 hole diameters.
2. The residuals are NOISE, not design. Per-hole residual VECTORS in plate coordinates are uncorrelated between the two well-conditioned photos: cos(angle) per hole = -0.59, +0.70, -0.77, +0.27, -0.34, -0.22, mean -0.160. A real design offset would give cos ~ +1 in every photo. The p0/p04 mean residual vector per hole is only 0.035–0.070 mm long with a half-range of comparable size (B2 0.035+-0.022/0.059; B3 0.060+-0.028/0.006; B1 0.045+-0.034/0.083; S2 0.057+-0.043/0.006; S1 0.070+-0.030/0.084; F 0.066+-0.042/0.070), i.e. no hole shows a significant systematic displacement.
3. Detection power. From the synthetic power curve (resid RMS ~ 0.021 + 0.21*delta at the ideal noise floor), a 0.5 mm single-hole design difference produces 0.106 mm and a 0.3 mm difference 0.063 mm. Our observed 0.082–0.097 mm sits at a REAL noise floor higher than the synthetic 0.011–0.028 mm, so I bound any single-hole design difference conservatively at <= 0.4 mm from the homography alone, and at <= ~0.15 mm (2 sigma) from the cross-photo consistency test, which is the tighter and more trustworthy bound because it cancels the per-photo noise.
4. The 5.5k-point outline residual (0.206–0.224 mm rms about a median of |<=0.078| mm) is an INDEPENDENT confirmation with hundreds of degrees of freedom, since none of those points entered the fit. The near-zero global median means the plate outline and the hole rims are the correct SIZE relative to the hole pattern — the whole plate's proportions match, not merely six points.
5. Anisotropy. From p0 (the only well-conditioned view) |r1|/|r2| = 0.9947–0.9986 against a synthetic null of 1.0086+-0.0054, so |kx/kz - 1| <~ 1.5%. The real plate is not a differently-proportioned design.

VERDICT ON PLATE IDENTITY: CONFIRMED. In three independent photographs the real web plate's hole pattern, hole rims and full outline are projectively identical to gripper_link.stl's web plate, with registration residual ~0.10 mm RMS / 0.15 mm max in the two well-conditioned views. The other lenses' assumption that they are photographing the same plate design as the asset is valid.
result.caveats:
ERROR SOURCES I COULD NOT ELIMINATE, QUANTIFIED:

1. ABSOLUTE SCALE IS UNOBSERVABLE BY CONSTRUCTION. Every quantity here is projective/dimensionless, so a uniform scale s is exactly degenerate with the homography. Verified explicitly in synthetic: s=1.00, 1.03 and 1.10 all give the same residual RMS (0.021, 0.021, 0.022 mm). This lens therefore contributes ZERO information about s, rho_real, or the 1.0302 breakeven. That is by design, not a failure.

2. THE 6-POINT HOMOGRAPHY ABSORBS ALL AFFINE DISTORTION. Verified: a design stretched 3% in x only gives residual RMS 0.0210 mm vs a null of 0.0206 mm — completely invisible. So the hole-centre residual alone tests only ~4 of the design's shape degrees of freedom. I partially closed this with (a) the EXIF-intrinsics metric check (bounds anisotropy to ~1.5%, but only p0 is well-conditioned) and (b) the 5.5k-point outline test. A design differing from the asset by a pure affine map with anisotropy under ~1.5% would still evade this lens.

3. HOLE-WALL OCCLUSION (plate thickness 1.510 mm). At view angle theta the far rim occludes up to t*tan(theta) of the opening — up to 0.4 mm at the plate corners. Synthetic modelling shows this is 97–99% common-mode (a uniform translation / radial shrink about the principal point) so it cancels in pairwise distances, leaving <=0.18% ratio error. It does NOT cancel in absolute hole diameters (see 4).

4. HOLE-DIAMETER MEASUREMENTS ARE UNUSABLE, so the attractive "fastener holes are a fixed absolute size" discriminator FAILED. Measured/asset apparent radius ratios scattered 0.90–1.13 (p0), 0.89–1.11 (p04), 0.64–1.32 (p02); d(B)/d(S) came out 1.636 (p0), 1.713 (p04), 1.955 (p02) against the asset's 1.4546 — i.e. +12% to +34% high. Causes: wall occlusion, per-hole illumination/shadow differences, powder-coat thickness, and unknown chamfer/burr. Moreover the effect I would need to see is tiny: a 3% pattern scale with unchanged M3 holes changes the hole radius by only 0.046 mm in the rectified frame, ~6x below the outline-test noise. Do NOT let any downstream lens use my radius numbers to infer s.

5. FLOWER FULL-CONTOUR ICP: ATTEMPTED AND DISCARDED AS INVALID. Otsu segmentation of the flower broke at its thin necks, capturing only 19.55 mm of the true 28.275 mm z-extent in p0 and 26.66 mm in p04. The resulting "flower scale" figures (0.786 / 0.790 / 0.958) are segmentation artifacts, NOT measurements. They must not be quoted or used anywhere.

6. HANDEDNESS / WHICH JAW IS PHOTOGRAPHED IS UNDETERMINED. The asset web face equals its own mirror about z=-18.9335 to IoU 0.99919, so neither the hole pattern nor the outline can tell me whether the photographed jaw is the one modelled by gripper_link.stl or the opposite jaw. I did NOT open, read, stat or hash gripper_left_link.stl (forbidden). If the two jaws' webs are mirror images, my result transfers to both. If they are not, my statement is strictly "the photographed web plate has the same design as gripper_link.stl's web plate" — which is still the asset under dispute, but a reader wanting handedness certainty would need explicit approval to inspect gripper_left_link.stl.

7. LENS DISTORTION NOT MODELLED. EXIF carries no distortion coefficients and the Samsung JPEG pipeline applies its own undisclosed correction. Residual distortion over the ~700 px plate extent could plausibly contribute ~0.05 mm, i.e. up to half of the observed 0.10 mm residual. This inflates my residual and therefore makes my design-difference bound conservative, not optimistic.

8. FOCAL LENGTH IS ONLY KNOWN TO ~2%. EXIF FocalLengthIn35mmFilm=23 (an integer) gives f=2657.9 px but admits 22.5–23.5 mm, i.e. 2600–2716 px. Swept: the anisotropy figure moves by <0.001 for p0 and by ~0.005 for the oblique views, so this is not limiting for p0. Only the metric check (item 2) depends on f at all; the residuals and ratios do not.

9. MIXED ESTIMATORS. The five small holes use the validated half-max blob centroid; the flower bore uses a radial gradient-edge ellipse fit (the blob method returns the whole flower, not the bore). Their systematics differ. The flower residual is in family with the others in p0/p04 (0.087, 0.120 mm), but in p02 it is the worst point (0.466 mm). The 5-point fits excluding the flower give RMS 0.098/0.053/0.188 mm, so none of my conclusions depend on the flower.

10. SEEDS WERE PLACED BY EYE from gridded crops. Mitigated by iterating each estimator to convergence and by the 36-setting robustness sweep (seeds perturbed +-6 px, start radii 0.85–1.15x), which moved the residual RMS only from 0.096 to 0.194 mm (p0) and 0.070 to 0.353 mm (p04).

11. ONLY THREE PHOTOS USED. p01, p03, p05 were rejected for steep obliquity / partial occlusion of the head. p02 was retained but is markedly worse (tilt ~25 deg, RMS 0.298 mm) and I weight it least; the quantitative claims rest on p0 and p04.

12. MY SYNTHETIC NULL (0.011–0.028 mm) UNDERSTATES REAL NOISE by 4–10x because it omits paint texture, speculars, burrs, real hole non-circularity, background clutter and JPEG artifacts. I therefore used it only for RELATIVE power/blindness statements, never as the absolute noise floor; absolute bounds come from the cross-photo consistency test instead.

13. THE RULER WAS NOT USED AT ALL, as required. None of the ruler traps (mm vs 1/32 in, the 96.4->101.3 px pitch gradient, rule-vs-plate height difference) can affect this lens, and equally this lens cannot cross-check them.

(1) SCENE PARSE. p04 is NOT "part standing with rule flat below": both the part and the rule stand against a beige backdrop, resting on a common plane; the blue/grey band at the bottom of the frame is the second surface at the junction. Apex points DOWN in the image (not left). Confirmed from bottom.png, shadow.png.

(2) HOLE DETECTION (two independent estimators, no threshold-only shortcut). (a) Subpixel radial max-gradient edge on 360 rays + IRLS circle fit, iterated (holes.py). (b) Local bimodal threshold T=(p8+p92)/2 + connected-component centroid, iterated (holes2.py). Only the 5 clean circular holes B1,B3,S1,S2,B2 were used. The "flower" was deliberately EXCLUDED from the metric fit: the lead supplied only its area centroid, not its inscribed-circle centre, and the physical part carries a lit deburr bevel that biases any radius-derived quantity.

(3) SCALE / POSE. Similarity (Umeyama, reflection allowed) for a first-order k, full affine for anisotropy, then planar PnP (SOLVEPNP_ITERATIVE, K = [f,0,cx;0,f,cy;0,0,1]) for the real answer. PnP is what the final number uses, because it removes the perspective term that a plain px/mm ratio cannot.

(4) RULER — TRAP 1 (unit identity). Found TWO interleaved tick families on the left of the rule: A at x∈[1718,1752], B at x∈[1762,1845]. Family B identified as MILLIMETRES by a period-10 long-tick + engraved-numeral pattern (long ticks at tick indices 3,13,23,33; "10/20/30/40" glyphs at 4-6,14-16,24-26,34-36). Family A is the 1/32-inch scale: measured pitch ratio A/B = 0.7877 vs the 0.79375 predicate, the residual 0.8% being a real 1.0-1.3 mm depth offset between two stacked blades of the digital angle rule. q was taken from family B only.

(5) RULER — TRAP 2 (perspective gradient). Did NOT assume a global px/mm. Tick centres extracted subpixel in three narrow x-bands, tick-line slope fitted (dy/dx=0.0303), each tick interpolated to a common reference column x=1790, then a 1-D projective model y(n)=(b+nq)/(1+nr) fitted in normalised coordinates. From (p=a·r, q, r) with |D|=1 mm, the rule's absolute 3-D line is recovered: Z0 and unit direction D.

(6) RULER — TRAP 3 (height offset). Handled by geometry, not assumption. Read the SOURCE STL (local_assets/roarm_m3/urdf/meshes/gripper_link.stl, sha256 7946a374…65a56 verified, rho_asset reproduced = 67.34892 at (67.0826,-5.9834,-20.8551)) to obtain the part's true 3-D structure: web sheet y∈[-5.983,-4.473]; two Z-normal tines at z∈[-38.617,-37.117] and z∈[-0.750,+0.750], each spanning y∈[-10.000,+15.240]. The 6-hole web pattern is exactly mirror-symmetric about z=-18.9335, so the holes alone CANNOT tell which web face is toward the camera — the tines can. Rendered both hypotheses through the fitted pose and compared silhouette edges against the photo (render2.py, ov_H1/ov_H2). Result: tines point TOWARD the camera. That fixes the web's standoff above the resting plane, which is the whole systematic.

(7) FINAL. s = (Z_rule_mm_face(at plate's image height) + ΔZ) / Z_plate(model units), with ΔZ from the STL-derived seating geometry. Grid-searched over f∈{2500,2555.6,2600,2650,2680}, principal point ±(30,40) px, and both hole estimators.
